prediction.whatIsNeededForEstimate: To compute a real dollar range I need: (1) the square footage of Shaw's office condominium unit (you gave the $275/sf rate but no area to apply it to); (2) the purchase price allocated to Shaw's unit in the August 2015 Mostafavi transaction — pull it from the closing/settlement statement, since expectancy damages are value minus that price; (3) an appraised or comparable-sales fair market value for the unit as of August 2015; (4) the unit's current appraised value if you intend to press the post-breach appreciation theory; (5) whether the lease contains a prevailing-party attorney-fee clause and the fees incurred to date; and (6) whether the lease contains a non-waiver clause, which directly affects the strength of the acquiescence defense.
prediction.likelyOutcome: Liability for breach of the right of first refusal is effectively conceded and the ten-year Iowa limitations period defeats the delay-as-time-bar argument, so the landlord's realistic outcomes are a complete defense verdict on estoppel by acquiescence (a genuine but not dominant chance) or, more likely, a finding of breach with nominal or sharply limited damages because the tenant has not proven an August 2015 value-versus-offer-price spread and his seven years of post-breach 'appreciation' is both wrongly measured and speculative. Expect a modest judgment against A & M rather than a large one, with attorney-fee entitlement potentially exceeding the compensatory award.

outcome.description: After a bench trial the district court awarded the tenant $257,216 in damages plus post-judgment interest, using the tenant's damages methodology (unrealized appreciation, rent-versus-mortgage differential, lost principal) but valuing the unit at the $166.73 per square foot the third-party buyers paid rather than the $275 the tenant proposed. No attorney's fees. The Iowa Court of Appeals affirmed (2-1) on August 19, 2026, rejecting the estoppel-by-acquiescence and failure-to-mitigate defenses.
